Normal knee joint alignment.   No fracture is seen.  
  No osteocartilagenous lesion is detected.  
  No focal bone marrow edema is noted.  
  Minimal amount of joint effusion is seen.  
  
  MCL is intact.  Small peripheral vertical tear at posterior horn of the medial meniscus is noted.  
  FCL, popliteus and biceps femoris tendons are preserved.       
   Normal shape with preserved signal of the lateral meniscus is observed.   
  
  Normal course with preserved signal of the ACL is noted.  The PCL is intact.  
  PF joint surface is preserved.   No subchondral bone lesion is noted.  
   Quadriceps and patellar tendons are preserved.  Small peripheral vertical tear at posterior horn of the medial meniscus.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Large lipohemarthrosis. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Normal.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Normal.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Normal.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Osteochondral fracture of the distal aspect of the medial facet of the patella with the displaced fragment measuring up to 15 mm, seen anterior to the lateral femoral condyle. Full-thickness chondral fissuring involving the patellar apex with chondral delamination of the medial facet.
Non-displaced small osteochondral fracture of the anterolateral aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. Findings are compatible lateral patellar fracture dislocation.
Mild thickening of the lateral patellar retinaculum with subtle irregularity at the patellar attachment compatible with low-grade partial-thickness tear.
The medial patellar retinaculum is intact. The extensor mechanism is intact.

Bones:
See above.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.Large volume lipohemarthrosis.
2.Lateral patellar fracture dislocation, with a displaced osteochondral fracture arising from the distal aspect of the medial facet, with the fragment anterior to the lateral femoral condyle. There is a contrecoup nondisplaced small osteochondral fracture of the anterolateral aspect of the lateral femoral condyle.
3.Full-thickness chondral fissuring of the patellar apex with delamination of the medial facet.
4.Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the lateral patellar retinaculum.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Rule out meniscal tear.

PRIOR IMAGING: Plain film radiographs from [Date]
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact and unremarkable. The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and unremarkable.

Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained.

T-TG distance is normal.

Lateral meniscus is intact. There is focal anterior and lateral femoral sulcus indentation with minor loss of cartilage of the lateral femoral condyle in the region of the sulcal depression. Overall articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

There is an oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus associated with a small posterior parameniscal cyst measuring about 4 to 5 mm in short axis tracking about 3 cm along the posterior margin of the meniscus and extending posterior to the base of the posterior cruciate ligament. Articular cartilage in the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus tendon and biceps femoris tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is significant edema and soft tissue stranding extending from the space between the medial head of gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscle proximally into the popliteal fossa behind the distal femur and distally into the medial soft tissues of the calf deep to the pes anserine tendons. The finding is consistent with a ruptured Baker's cyst.

There is no significant knee effusion.

INTERPRETATION: 

Oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the medial meniscus involving body and posterior horn with associated para meniscal cyst posteriorly.

Nonacute osteochondral impaction injury involving lateral femoral sulcus with some mild focal cartilage loss overlying the region of cortical depression. No associated anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Soft tissue edema compatible with ruptured Baker's cyst.

Lateral femoral kondil ile tibyal plato posterolateralindeki kemik kontüzyonları lateral femoral kondildeki impaksiyon kırığı ile birlikte. Lateral femoral kondil posteriyorundaki kemik adası 5 mm çaplı. Diz eklemi içi sıvı miktarı hafif derecede artmış. Arka çapraz ve yan bağlar normal. Ön çapraz bağ ödemli olup posterolateral demet düzeyinde parsiyel yırtık izleniyor. Yırtık lifler anteriyor interkondiler çentiğe deplase olmuş. Medyal menisküsün gövde kesimindeki serbest kenar ondülasyonuna meniskokapsüler bağ yırtığı eşlik ediyor (tip 1 rampa lezyonu). Lateral menisküs normal. Eklem kıkırdakları ve kemikler normal. Ekstensör mekanizma korunmuş. Proksimal tibyofibular eklem normal.

МР находка: МР данни за стрес фрактура под главата на фибулата. Няма данни за дислокация. Изобразява се фрактурна линия през напречника на костта, около която се вижда изразен оток на костния мозък.  Тибия, патела – с нормална форма. Наличие на малък контузионен костно-мозъчен едем в медиалния кондил на фемура. Няма данни за ставен излив. Нормално изобразяване на менискусите. Кръстните връзки са със запазена цялост. Ставният хрущял е интактен. Колатерални лигаменти – без особености. Ретинакулуми – б.о. Лигамент на пателата, сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис – без особености. Заключение: MР данни за стрес фрактура на фибулата. Не се намират други патологични изменения в дясното коляно.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 64-year-old with progressive left knee pain related to "wear and tear". Evaluate for cartilage loss. Evaluate for meniscus tear.
Comparison: No recent left lower extremity imaging available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee is acquired in 3 anatomic planes at 1.2 Tesla using a local extremity receiver coil and a noncontrast protocol.

FINDINGS:

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Osseous and articular alignment at the left knee are normal.
No fracture. No focal osseous contusion.
No evidence for a recent pivot shift mechanism.

JOINT SPACE:
There is a small left knee effusion.
There is a minimal, partially ruptured Baker's cyst.
No intra-articular bodies.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a complex tear of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with a dominant oblique undersurface component and a smaller inner margin radial component at the junction posterior horn and posterior root. There is moderate subsequent medial meniscus extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss all along the weightbearing region of the medial femoral condyle, with focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial femoral margin.
There is partial-thickness cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: The lateral meniscus shows normal morphology and signal with no tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage throughout the lateral tibiofemoral compartment is normal.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
There is a small region of focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge, with more diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss extending along the medial patellar facet.
There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss with deep chondral fissuring at the central femoral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal morphology and signal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): The MCL is bowed from medial meniscus extrusion, but intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: The fibular-collateral ligament and anterolateral ligament are normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Intact stabilizers.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with intrasubstance degeneration at its patellar attachment and mild enthesopathy. No high-grade quadriceps tear.
Patella tendon: Normal morphology and signal with no tear or degeneration.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No significant soft tissue edema in Hoffa's fat.
A TT-TG distance is normal at 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
The distal iliotibial band and biceps femoris are normal.
The distal semimembranosus is normal.

SOFT TISSUES:
Neurovascular structures in the popliteal fossa are normal.
Subcutaneous soft tissues are normal. No soft tissue mass.

IMPRESSION:

1. Extensive complex medial meniscus tear with a dominant oblique undersurface component at its body and posterior horn, moderate medial meniscus extrusion, and high-grade cartilage loss on the medial femoral condyle with low-grade cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

2. Focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge with high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the central femoral trochlea.

3. Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with mild enthesopathy.

4. Small left knee effusion with a minimal ruptured Baker's cyst.
